Research problem: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

Below are 24 candidate research ideas for this problem. Group them into 4-7 method families such that ideas in the same family share their core mechanism (not merely their goal). Give each family a short name.

[A1-g0-C1] Asymmetric patch-level MIL with a SigLIP loss for mask-free segmentation adapters
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters from image labels only: every patch of a normal image is pushed to the normal anchor and the top-2% patches of an abnormal image to the abnormal anchor, with a sigmoid (SigLIP-style) patch-text loss at all four levels.

[A1-g0-C2] Detection-to-segmentation pseudo-mask self-distillation
Use the image-label-trained detection branch's multi-level patch maps, filtered by cross-level agreement, as pseudo-masks to train the segmentation branch with MVFA's existing Dice and Focal losses, iterating twice.

[A1-g0-C3] Hybrid supervision: synthetic-mask segmentation loss plus real-image MIL
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters with Dice + Focal on synthetic anomalies pasted into normal source images and a top-k MIL loss on real image-labelled abnormal images, removing all expert masks.

[A1-g0-C4] DINO-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
Train with image-level MIL first, then refine the resulting patch maps of abnormal source images by random-walk propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph into pseudo-masks that supervise MVFA's segmentation adapters.

[A1-g0-C5] Two-stage anomaly-aware anchors then patch MIL, all from image labels
Stage 1 learns residual text adapters that separate normal and abnormal anchors using image-level labels and an orthogonality term; stage 2 trains MVFA's segmentation adapters with top-k patch MIL against the frozen stage-1 anchors.

[A1-g0-C6] Graph-Laplacian smoothness regularisation for MIL-trained segmentation adapters
Add to the image-level MIL loss a feature-weighted graph-Laplacian smoothness term on each level's patch anomaly map, so localisation learned from image labels forms coherent regions.

[A1-g1-o1] Normal-bank pseudo-masks: localising anomalies in image-labelled source data by distance to that dataset's normal patches
Use the image labels of each source dataset to build a memory bank of its normal patches, mark patches of its abnormal images that are far from every normal patch as pseudo-anomalous, and train MVFA's segmentation adapters with Dice and Focal on these pseudo-masks.

[A1-g1-o2] Attribution-based pseudo-masks: gradient attribution of the detection branch's image score supervises the segmentation adapters
Keep the detection-to-segmentation teacher idea but replace the detection branch's mean-pooled patch maps with Grad-CAM-style attributions of its image-level score to the patch tokens, filtered across levels, as pseudo-masks.

[A1-g1-o3] Cross-branch co-training of MVFA's detection and segmentation adapters from image labels
Let MVFA's two adapter branches supervise each other: confident patches of each branch's map become pseudo-labels for the other, while image labels anchor both, so neither branch alone determines the pseudo-masks.

[A1-g1-o4] Counterfactual patch replacement: learning where anomalies are from which patches, when replaced by normal tissue, flip the image decision
For each abnormal source image, replace each patch's adapted feature by its nearest neighbour from that dataset's normal-patch bank and measure the drop in the image-level anomaly score; patches with the largest counterfactual drop become pseudo-masks for the segmentation adapters.

[A1-g1-o5] Anomaly-aware anchors with patch MIL and DINO-affinity-refined pseudo-masks for mask-free segmentation adapters
Learn anomaly-aware text anchors from image labels, train the segmentation adapters with top-k MIL against them, then grow the resulting MIL maps into pseudo-masks over a DINOv2 affinity graph for a final Dice/Focal stage.

[A1-g1-o6] Cross-image MIL ranking for mask-free segmentation, borrowed from weakly supervised video anomaly detection
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters with a ranking loss that requires the top patch scores of every abnormal image to exceed the top patch scores of normal images from the same dataset in the same mini-batch, plus sparsity and smoothness terms, using only image labels.

[A1-g2-o1] Context-surprisal pseudo-masks: a masked feature predictor trained on normal images flags patches it cannot predict
Train a small transformer to predict masked patch tokens from their context on normal source images only; on abnormal images, patches whose tokens are poorly predicted from surrounding tissue form pseudo-masks for MVFA's segmentation adapters.

[A1-g2-o2] Change detection against a retrieved normal twin: optimal-transport pseudo-masks from image labels
For each abnormal source image, retrieve its most similar normal image from the same dataset, align their patch tokens with entropic optimal transport, and treat the patch mass of the abnormal image that cannot be transported cheaply as the pseudo-mask for MVFA's segmentation adapters.

[A1-g2-o3] Attribution-proposed, counterfactual-verified pseudo-masks for mask-free segmentation adapters
Use gradient attribution of the detection branch's image score to propose candidate anomalous patches cheaply, keep only those whose counterfactual replacement by the nearest normal-bank patch lowers the image score, and train the segmentation adapters on the verified pseudo-masks.

[A1-g2-o4] Position-aware normal-bank pseudo-masks: matching each patch only to normal patches from the same anatomical neighbourhood
Keep normal-bank pseudo-masks from image labels but substitute global nearest-neighbour search with a neighbourhood-restricted search over normal patches at the same grid position (+/- 2 patches), so anatomy that is normal elsewhere cannot hide an anomaly.

[A1-g2-o5] Adversarial erasing for full lesion extent: iterative MIL that must still find the anomaly after its most obvious part is erased
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters with image-level MIL in rounds; after each round, erase (replace by normal-bank tokens) the top-scoring region of each abnormal training image and require the remaining patches to still carry anomaly evidence, so localisation grows from the most discriminative patches to the whole lesion.

[A1-g2-o6] Patch-level positive-unlabelled learning: normal-image patches as labelled negatives, abnormal-image patches as unlabelled
Recast mask-free training of MVFA's segmentation adapters as positive-unlabelled (PU) learning at the patch level, using the non-negative PU risk estimator with a per-dataset class prior (expected lesion fraction) estimated from image-labelled data.

[A1-g3-o1] Equivariance-regularised MIL: geometric consistency as free supervision for mask-free segmentation adapters
Add to asymmetric MIL a self-supervised constraint that the segmentation map of a geometrically transformed image equals the transformed map of the original, which pushes MIL's sparse, most-discriminative activations to cover whole lesions.

[A1-g3-o2] Noisy-label learning with small-loss selection: all abnormal-image patches as noisy positives
Label every patch of an abnormal image as abnormal and every patch of a normal image as normal, then learn MVFA's segmentation adapters with small-loss selection (co-teaching between two adapter copies) so the many mislabelled normal patches inside abnormal images are progressively ignored.

[A1-g3-o3] Bank-informed positive-unlabelled learning: patch-specific class priors from position-aware normal-bank distances
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters with non-negative PU learning, but replace the single dataset-level class prior with patch-specific priors derived from position-aware normal-bank distances, so likely-lesion patches carry more of the unlabelled positive mass.

[A1-g3-o4] Rank-atlas MIL: selecting MIL positives by per-position empirical-CDF normalisation of normal scores
Replace the positional mean/std atlas with a per-position empirical CDF of normal-image scores, so MIL positives are the patches whose score is most extreme relative to normal images at the same location, robust to skewed and heavy-tailed score distributions.

[A1-g3-o5] Bank-gated asymmetric MIL: positives must be both text-abnormal and unlike any normal patch of the dataset
In asymmetric SigLIP-MIL, choose the positive patches of an abnormal image only among those that the dataset's normal-patch bank also flags as unusual, and use the bank distance as a soft target weight, combining text-based and memory-based evidence from image labels.

[A1-g3-o6] Optimal-transport label assignment of abnormal mass to patches under a lesion-fraction budget
Assign the 'abnormal' label of each abnormal training image to its patches by entropic optimal transport, with a mass budget equal to the dataset's estimated lesion fraction and costs from the current segmentation scores, as modern object detectors assign labels to anchors.
